reasons.reader_question: The beat's question ('Why hasn't he searched the bales?') is answered in the penultimate paragraph ('If he followed the medicine, it might lead him to the hand behind it'), so the gap closes before the reader leaves. What remains open is vaguer: whether Rohan will spot that the guide is the Fox.
reasons.change: Knowledge shifts: he now holds a redbark trace and is knowingly harbouring a load. Power shifts: she forces her way onto the crossing, keeps her name, and wins the argument in front of her village. Control turns to compromise, as the beat asks.
reasons.romance_movement: Both required turns land for new reasons. He respects her choice to walk a killing pass for Jassi ('He knew that sum'), and she watches him leave Puja's step with no way to explain it. The yard debate also moves his judgement ('a man explaining a noose').
reasons.shown_chemistry: Strong responsive details: she counts his stride and the count skips when he nears the bale; she refuses her name with 'It's the one you can prove'; she watches from the door. Two spots slip into narration: 'he found he did not want hers by force, not yet' and the closing gloss on 'Captain'.
reasons.character_logic: Rohan is mostly sharp, and leaving the bale so he can follow it is smart. Three slips: he lets 'I haven't told you one false word' pass, though she lied to him in ch1 about Jassi's chest and deafness; he has read a 'sealed' order 'until the words went smooth'; and he deduces an ear from cartilage although Kiran's ear in ch1 is blackened, not missing.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The next decision costs something. By his own law, letting the load cross puts him on the same rope as a goatherd, and 'you may not come back' sits over Jassi on the eve of ch3. Varun's gully choice quietly arms the avalanche.
reasons.prose: Clean, concrete and readable, with no banned phrases, AI tells or em dashes, and good lines ('It hanged a man for crossing and let him keep the rope'). Weaknesses: three scenes in a row end on silence ('Neither of them said a word', 'said nothing'), echoing ch1's 'did not say anything at all'; 'He might have said something' and 'He walked past' open consecutive paragraphs; and 'said the woman from the doorway' clashes with 'come up behind him'.
reasons.continuity: Consistent with the bible and ch1: Jassi is forty with old-knees jokes, Puja's son matches, the mother died ten winters ago, Dilan was 23, the brass button with its stiff shank matches the drop token, Varun says 'Captain-ji', and the pairing matches F057. The cartilage detail is a risk to watch, not yet a conflict.

fixes: At 'If he followed the medicine, it might lead him to the hand behind it', the planned Shaped Gap closes on the page: the chapter answers its own outgoing question. Cut that sentence and 'But the powder was going where the Fox's crew was going'. Keep the harbouring line, then add a half-answer that widens the gap, such as his hand going to the sealed order's line ('delivered, not hanged'), so the reader leaves asking what he is planning.

At 'I haven't told you one false word. Count them', she lied to him in ch1 ('cold in his chest... deaf in the left ear'), and a smart Rohan who has just watched Jassi answer him lets it pass (Irrational behaviour to extend plot). Add one beat where Rohan silently counts that first lie, for example noting that Jassi heard him from across the yard. This plants the lie theme before the bond in ch3 and sharpens 'a guide who would not lie to his face'. Alternatively, make her line 'not one false word since you came up the stair'.

At 'a curl of frozen cartilage no longer than a fingernail', the report implies a missing piece of ear, but ch1 gives Kiran an ear 'black along the rim'. Change it to the beat's 'torn frozen skin', for example 'a scrap of skin frozen to the ice, torn from the rim of an ear', and adjust 'A man who loses the rim of an ear' to 'A man whose ear froze to the ice'. While there, fix 'a second paper, sealed... he had read until the words went smooth' to 'its seal broken once and pressed flat since'.
reader_question: Rohan has smelled redbark on the guides' packs and let it cross, so whose hand is behind the load, and what will it cost him when he finds out it is hers?
new_facts_assessment: The Dilan report (blood plus a fingernail curl of frozen cartilage, read as an ear rim) is necessary for C03, but it implies a missing piece of ear. Ch1 shows Kiran's ear as 'black along the rim', which reads as still attached. Use the beat's 'torn frozen skin' so later scenes don't contradict it. The Closing Law harbouring fact is necessary and consistent with F016, and it gives this chapter its cost. The bales standing in the goat pen and being searched last is consistent with ch1 and F055. One unlisted new fact needs recording: the queen wants the Fox 'delivered and not hanged'. It is fine and useful, but it belongs in new-facts.json.
